summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for a flare of chronic pancreatitis, presenting with severe abdominal pain, nausea, and inability to tolerate oral intake. She was managed with her established IV pain and nausea regimen, kept NPO initially, and gradually advanced to full oral intake and J tube use by day six. On hospital day four, she developed fever and erythema at her peripheral IV site, diagnosed as thrombophlebitis; IV vancomycin was given briefly but discontinued after resolution and negative blood cultures. Imaging revealed a chronic thrombosis in the right internal jugular vein. Warfarin was held on admission due to supratherapeutic INR and poor intake, with enoxaparin bridging initiated once INR was subtherapeutic. Hypertension was managed with IV metoprolol as needed, and lisinopril was restarted at discharge. Depression and anxiety were addressed with reinstitution of amitriptyline and a short course of Ativan. A port placement was arranged outpatient for future access. She improved clinically and was discharged home on her baseline medications, enoxaparin, and instructions to monitor INR.
problems: Phlebitis and thrombophlebitis of other sites
Acute venous embolism and thrombosis of internal jugular veins
Acute upper respiratory infections of unspecified site
